To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the labour demand model is consistent with a dynamic adjustment cost model with forward-looking behaviour, and the estimated parameters are economically meaningful.

(1) the dynamic model is able to explain the behaviour of the labour market variables, (2) the model is well specified in terms of the cointegrated system and the VEqCM and (3) it is possible to test and estimate the model using a switching algorithm.

(i) the dynamic adjustment cost model with forward-looking agents and cointegration is an appropriate modelling framework to analyse dynamic labour demand, (ii) the estimated model provides a good fit to the data and (iii) the estimated model can be used to test hypotheses on labour demand behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of dynamic adjustment cost models where forward looking agents choose a set (or vector) of non-stationar variables.
the development of a new approach for modelling dynamic adjustment cost models with forward-looking behaviour.
dynamic adjustment cost models where forward looking agents choose a non-stationary set of variables subject to quadratic costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this book provides a very useful and interesting contribution to the field of dynamic adjustment cost models.
, in general, the paper provides a useful extension of the standard adjustment cost models, and it is a valuable contribution to the literature on dynamic models of adjustment.
the results of this paper are not only theoretically interesting and important, but also empirically relevant for the labour market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an estimation method for dynamic adjustment cost models with forward-looking behaviour and applied it to a labour demand model for Danish manufacturing industries.
we have shown that the dynamic decision problem of a forward-looking agent subject to quadratic adjustment cost can be solved by a VEqCM.
we propose a new method for dynamic decision problems with forward-looking behaviour, where expectations are computed by an equilibrium correction model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic adjustment cost model with forward-looking expectations can be used as an empirical model.
the dynamic adjustment cost model can be used as an alternative to the standard partial adjustment model in empirical applications.
the VEqCM is a flexible framework to model forward-looking behaviour and adjustment costs in the context of non-stationarity.
